result.title: Learning Grounded Reasoning from Human Gaze
result.summary: Human visual reasoning is driven by systematic exploration and extraction of task-relevant visual evidence. Human gaze provides a window into this process, making gaze a useful source of guidance for visually-grounded reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs). However, human gaze also includes noise and redundancies that may transfer poorly to VLMs. In this work, we investigate how human gaze data can be effectively leveraged to improve visual reasoning in VLMs, while maintaining alignment with human behavior. We collect 7,109 human gaze trials from a diverse and challenging set of visual reasoning tasks, and train grounded reasoning models with different forms of gaze guidance. Across evaluations in chart understanding, visual search, and counting, we find that using human gaze as a prior for grounded reasoning consistently outperforms supervision using the full gaze sequence. Based on these findings, we introduce GGR (Gaze-Guided Reasoner), which achieves greater human alignment and more reliable visual grounding while matching or outperforming leading grounded-reasoning baselines in accuracy. Reinforcement learning further improves task accuracy, gaze alignment, and grounding quality despite using no gaze supervision. Behavioral analyses show that gaze supervised models exhibit more visual exploration before arriving at an answer. Our results suggest that the value of human gaze lies in guiding spatial exploration and shaping reasoning behavior without requiring complete imitation of human behavior.

AI.brief_summary: 该文收集 7,109 条人类注视轨迹，比较整段注视序列与作为先验的注视引导，并提出 GGR，使 VLM 在图表理解、视觉搜索和计数中兼顾答案准确率、人类对齐与视觉定位。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究直接触及视觉证据筛选与探索行为塑造，其“用注视先验而非完整模仿”的结论可供核查 LVR 中视觉旁路、证据选择监督和 LOOK 成本之间的权衡。
